subject: <Your-Repo>
$comment: TEMPLATE: copy to <repo>/proofs/modules.json, set `subject`, and replace the `modules` array with one entry per model. The array is the leg's ROSTER, and the only one: `check.ps1` reads the modules it checks from it, in its order, so a model follows every module it opens. Each entry's `kind` is `extracted` (checked, extracted to the oracle, diffed), `proofOnly` or `generated` (checked only) or `shared` (a module every model opens, such as `Twin` and `ListAlgebra` copied from the reference repository: checked first and extracted), and its `opens` lists the registered modules its code references. What the proof leg COSTS, declared per module, so that a growth in prover time is named rather than discovered when CI times out: every green CHECK line prints the module's measured seconds beside its `budgetSeconds`, and an overshoot is a recorded COST finding, never a red leg. How the leg reads every number in this file — the budget and its both-ways coverage, the cached-read threshold and each entry's `fastestSeconds`, the contention factor and its label — is stated once, in the kit engine's header (`check-proof-leg.ps1`). This is NOT `proofs.json`: a wall-clock budget is a claim at none of the ladder's levels. Hand-authored; the seeding rules below say how a number is arrived at, and bumping one is a recorded act.

seeding.rule: budgetSeconds = max(2 x the slowest observed cold-cache run, minimumBudgetSeconds), rounded up to the next 10s.
seeding.$comment: The tolerance is applied ONCE, here, when a number is seeded — `check.ps1` multiplies nothing, so the pair it prints is the measurement against the ceiling and there is no second arithmetic to hold in your head. Seed from the SLOWEST observed cold run rather than the median: concurrent sessions on one machine can inflate a cold check by ~1.8x with nothing about the tree changed, so a budget seeded from the median fires on a busy afternoon and teaches a reader to ignore it. `minimumBudgetSeconds` is the floor UNDER THE CEILING, for the sub-5s modules where 2x is inside ordinary process-start noise; it is a different thing from the per-module time floors this kit used to ship (retired by Phase 399 for `cachedRead`).

cachedRead.rule: thresholdSeconds = about twice the slowest CACHED read you measure on the pinned prover (cold-check a few modules into one cache, then re-run each against it with the leg's flags); appliesFromFastestSeconds = three times the threshold.
cachedRead.$comment: TEMPLATE: the numbers are the reference repository's (cached reads measured at 0.18-0.51s on its dev machine); measure your own, by `rule`. What the threshold does, and why one number serves every module, is stated once in the kit engine's header (`check-proof-leg.ps1`, step 1).

contentionSeeding.rule: threshold = a number above the median ratio of a measured QUIET pass on the SLOWEST machine that runs this leg, and at or below the median ratio of the contention worth naming. Place it high: a false label suppresses a real regression, where a missed label costs only what the leg did before.
contentionSeeding.quietFactor: <the median factor YOUR quiet pass measured — re-seed `threshold` from it>
contentionSeeding.$comment: TEMPLATE: the numbers here are the reference repository's, not a measurement of your leg — re-seed `threshold` and `quietFactor` from your own machines before trusting a label, by `rule`. What the factor is, what a label does, why its neutral point sits well below one, and what `minimumSamples`, `minimumSeconds` and an entry's optional `contentionFactor` mean, is stated once in the kit engine's header (`check-proof-leg.ps1`, THE CONTENTION FACTOR and WHAT THE NUMBER'S SCALE ACTUALLY IS).

modules.note: One entry per model. `measuredSeconds` is the observation the budget was seeded from and `fastestSeconds` the fastest genuine cold check observed, which decides whether the cached-read threshold applies — keep both, because a bump is only readable against the number it replaced. An OPTIONAL `contentionFactor` may sit beside `measuredSeconds`: the contention factor the leg reported on the pass that measurement came from, so a later reader can tell a budget seeded quiet from one seeded busy. It is provenance only, never computed with, and an absent one reads as `not recorded` rather than as 1 — which is why this worked entry does not carry one. The note says what the module is, what makes it expensive or cheap, and anything a future reader must check BEFORE reading a bump as ordinary growth (a scoped `--z3rlimit`, an `--ext context_pruning` that could have been lost, an SMT-pattern cliff).
